Prerequisite: Certificates from the DoD PKI (or another approved CA): a server certificate and private key for the FortiVoice services, the issuing root and intermediate CA certificates, and a client certificate where a server requires one
What it enables: DoD-issued certificates for HTTPS, SIP TLS, and SIP WSS, and validation of the certificates received from SIP TLS peers and trunks, LDAPS servers, RADIUS over TLS servers, and SMTP relays
How to put it in place: Generate a certificate signing request on the FortiVoice unit and have the CA sign it, or obtain a signed certificate; GUI: System > Certificate > Local Certificate (Import, then Assign to the service); GUI: System > Certificate > CA Certificate (Import the root and intermediate CA certificates)
Source: FortiVoice Phone System 8.0.0 Administration Guide, "Obtaining and installing a local certificate", "Managing CA certificates" (CA certificates validate the received certificate with TLS as SIP transport and authenticate RADIUS over TLS; the CA certificate CN must be the RADIUS server IP address), and "Configuring LDAP profiles" (client certificate signed by a CA whose certificate is imported)

Prerequisite: A current certificate revocation list (CRL) from the CA, or the certificate of the CA's OCSP server
What it enables: Revocation checking of the certificates that FortiVoice validates
How to put it in place: Download the CRL from the CA; GUI: System > Certificate > Certificate Revocation List (Import); GUI: System > Certificate > Remote (Import the OCSP server certificate)
Source: FortiVoice Phone System 8.0.0 Administration Guide, "Managing the certificate revocation list" (periodically upload a current CRL) and "Managing OCSP server certificates" (remote certificates are required if OCSP is enabled)

Prerequisite: An LDAP server (such as Microsoft Active Directory, OpenLDAP, Microsoft Entra Domain Services, or Google Workspace secure LDAP) with a bind account that can query the base DN, and for LDAPS its CA certificate (P1)
What it enables: LDAP authentication of administrators and extension users, and the LDAP contact list and connector
How to put it in place: Create the bind account on the LDAP server; GUI: Phone System > LDAP > LDAP Profile (Server name/IP, Secure Connection, Base DN, Bind DN)
Source: FortiVoice Phone System 8.0.0 Administration Guide, "Configuring LDAP profiles"; FortiVoice 8.0 Solution Guide, "LDAP authentication" (MS Active Directory or OpenLDAP; Integrating with Microsoft Entra Domain Services)

Prerequisite: A RADIUS server that accepts the FortiVoice unit as a client, with the users and any second factor managed on it, and for RADIUS over TLS (port 2183) its CA certificate (P1)
What it enables: RADIUS authentication of administrators and extension web access, and the token dialog in FortiFone Softclient
How to put it in place: Add the FortiVoice unit as a RADIUS client on the server; GUI: Phone System > Profile > RADIUS (Server name/IP, Server port, Server secret, Transport protocol TLS)
Source: FortiVoice 8.0 Solution Guide, "RADIUS authentication" (the RADIUS server must be configured to accept the FortiVoice phone system as a client; usernames and passwords are managed on the RADIUS server; upload CA certificates for TLS); FortiVoice Phone System 8.0.0 Administration Guide, "Configuring RADIUS authentication profiles"

Prerequisite: A SAML 2.0 identity provider (such as FortiAuthenticator, Google Workspace, or Microsoft 365) with the FortiVoice unit registered as a service provider, and the second factor (token by email or SMS) set up on it
What it enables: Single sign-on and two-factor authentication for the admin portal and the user portal
How to put it in place: Register the FortiVoice unit on the identity provider and exchange the SAML settings; GUI: Phone System > Single Sign On > Settings
Source: FortiVoice Phone System 8.0.0 Administration Guide, "Configuring single sign on" (FortiAuthenticator as the example authentication system); FortiVoice 8.0 Solution Guide, "Single sign-on authentication" (SAML 2.0 identity providers; Integrating with Google Workspace and Microsoft 365)

Prerequisite: Remote log servers: up to three syslog servers or FortiAnalyzer units reachable on UDP port 514
What it enables: Off-box storage of the FortiVoice logs
How to put it in place: GUI: Log & Report > Log Setting > Remote (IP, Port, Level, Facility)
Source: FortiVoice Phone System 8.0.0 Administration Guide, "Configuring logging to a Syslog server or FortiAnalyzer unit" (a maximum of three remote syslog servers; port 514 for FortiAnalyzer, UDP 514 by default for syslog)

Prerequisite: An SNMP manager with the Fortinet proprietary and supported standard MIBs compiled into it, and SNMP access enabled on the interface it uses
What it enables: SNMP queries and traps
How to put it in place: Compile the FortiVoice MIBs into the SNMP manager; GUI: System > Configuration > SNMP (SNMP v3 user with the manager address)
Source: FortiVoice Phone System 8.0.0 Administration Guide, "Configuring SNMP queries and traps" (compile the Fortinet MIBs into the SNMP manager; enable SNMP access on the network interfaces) and "FortiVoice MIBs"

Prerequisite: NTP servers reachable from the FortiVoice unit, preferably DoD NTP servers on the management network
What it enables: Synchronization of the system time, which logging, scheduling, and certificate features depend on, and the NTP server given to phones
How to put it in place: GUI: System > Configuration > Time (Synchronize with NTP Server)
Source: FortiVoice Phone System 8.0.0 Administration Guide, "Configuring the time and date" (for scheduling, logging, and certificate-dependent features the system time must be accurate)

Prerequisite: DNS servers for the VVoIP system, preferably on the local network
What it enables: Name resolution for the FortiVoice unit
How to put it in place: GUI: System > Network > DNS (Primary DNS server, Secondary DNS server)
Source: FortiVoice Phone System 8.0.0 Administration Guide, "Configuring DNS" (FortiVoice units require DNS servers; use DNS servers on the local network)

Prerequisite: An SMTP relay that accepts mail from the FortiVoice unit, with SSL/TLS support and an account on it
What it enables: Alert email, the daily security audit email, and other notifications
How to put it in place: GUI: System > Configuration > Mail Setting (Relay Server, Use SMTPs, Authentication Required, then Test)
Source: FortiVoice Phone System 8.0.0 Administration Guide, "Configuring email settings" (Relay Server; Use SMTPs must be enabled to initiate SMTPS connections) and "Managing CA certificates" (validate the email server certificate with STARTTLS)

Prerequisite: An SFTP (or FTP) server reachable from the FortiVoice unit, with an account and a directory
What it enables: Remote scheduled backups of the configuration and user data, and archiving of recorded calls
How to put it in place: Create the account and directory on the server; GUI: System > Maintenance > Configuration (Scheduled Backup, Remote backup); GUI: Call Feature > Call Recording > Archive (Destination: Remote)
Source: FortiVoice Phone System 8.0.0 Administration Guide, "Backing up the configuration" (scheduled backup to a remote FTP/SFTP server) and "Archiving recorded calls" (Remote: a remote FTP or SFTP storage server)

Prerequisite: An approved remote RESTful server (a CDR database or a customer relationship management system) with an account
What it enables: Submission of call detail records and call events off the FortiVoice unit
How to put it in place: Configure the database or CRM to receive the data; GUI: Log & Report > CDR > Submit CDR (Remote RESTful Server, Protocol, Authentication); GUI: Log & Report > Call Event > Server
Source: FortiVoice Phone System 8.0.0 Administration Guide, "Configuring CDR submission" (the configuration values should match those of the database server) and "Submitting call events to a remote RESTful server"

Prerequisite: Access switches that support 802.1Q VLAN tagging (and LLDP-MED for the LLDP option), with the voice and data VLANs configured
What it enables: VLAN subinterfaces on the FortiVoice unit and the voice and data VLAN tags pushed to the phones
How to put it in place: Configure the voice and data VLANs on the switches; GUI: System > Network > Network (VLAN interface); GUI: Phone System > Profile > Phone (VLAN)
Source: FortiVoice Phone System 8.0.0 Administration Guide, "VLAN subinterfaces" and "Configuring phone profiles" (VLAN: the network switch supports 802.1Q VLAN tagging and LLDP-MED)

Prerequisite: Phones with full TLS support: not the legacy FON-675i, FON-C71, FON-D71, FON-H25, or FON-H35, which have limited TLS support
What it enables: TLS transport and Secure RTP between the phones and the FortiVoice unit
How to put it in place: GUI: Phone System > Device > Phone (check the phone models); replace the legacy models
Source: FortiVoice 8.0 Solution Guide, "FortiVoice and FortiFone compatibility matrix" (Limited TLS support on legacy phone models)

Prerequisite: A SIP trunk from a VoIP service provider: registration credentials, and TLS and PIDF-LO where the provider supports them
What it enables: SIP trunk registration with credentials, encrypted trunk signaling, and location objects on emergency calls
How to put it in place: Order the trunk from the provider; GUI: Trunk > VoIP > SIP (Registration, Transport protocol, then Test)
Source: FortiVoice Phone System 8.0.0 Administration Guide, "Configuring VoIP trunks" (VoIP service providers deliver telephone services to SIP-based PBXs; Testing SIP trunks)

Prerequisite: The peer office PBX (a FortiVoice unit, or a third-party PBX for a custom peer), registered with this unit's IP address and SIP port
What it enables: Office peer trunks
How to put it in place: Configure the matching trunk on both systems; GUI: Trunk > Office Peer > Office Peer
Source: FortiVoice Phone System 8.0.0 Administration Guide, "Configuring office peers" (the FortiVoice unit and the peer office PBX must be mutually registered with each other's IP address and SIP port number)

Prerequisite: A second FortiVoice unit of the same model (or the matching VM type, with a second VM license) on the same firmware version, heartbeat interfaces connected directly or through a dedicated switch, a virtual IP address, and the licenses registered for HA (a perpetual license file with both serial numbers; subscriptions registered for each unit)
What it enables: Active-passive HA with configuration and data synchronization
How to put it in place: Connect the heartbeat interfaces; GUI: System > High Availability > Configuration (on each unit); GUI: System > High Availability > Status
Source: FortiVoice Phone System 8.0.0 Administration Guide, "About high availability" (same models, same firmware version, same hardware) and "Enabling and configuring HA"; FortiVoice 8.0 Solution Guide, "Planning high availability" (two VM licenses; FVE-500F with FVE-VM-500 but not FVE-200F8 with FVE-VM-200) and "Managing licenses in an HA deployment"

Prerequisite: FortiVoice local survivable gateway (LSG) units of a supported model (FVE-20E2, FVE-20E4, FVE-50E6, FVE-50G2, FVE-100E, FVE-100F, FVE-200F8, or FVE-500F), managed by a main office FortiVoice of model FVE-300E-T or larger or FVE-VM-500 or larger, over MPLS, a VPN, or SD-WAN
What it enables: Local survivability branches, the FXO and PRI gateways in them, and the settings pushed to them
How to put it in place: Deploy the LSG units (see the FortiVoice Local Survivable Gateway Deployment Guide); GUI: Managed System > Survivability
Source: FortiVoice Phone System 8.0.0 Administration Guide, "Configuring local survivability" (Supported models); FortiVoice 8.0 Solution Guide, "Supported local survivable gateway models" and "Local survivable gateway topology"

Prerequisite: FortiFone Softclient licenses (FVE-SCLIENT-10 or FVE-SCLIENT-100), registered and uploaded, and allocated to each extension that uses the softclient
What it enables: FortiFone Softclient for desktop and mobile on an extension, and the logs collected from it
How to put it in place: Register the license and download the license file in FortiCloud; GUI: Dashboard > Status (License Information widget, Update License); GUI: Extension > Extension > IP Extension (Soft FortiFone, License allocation)
Source: FortiVoice 8.0 Solution Guide, "FortiVoice add-on features" (Perpetual licenses: FortiFone Softclient), "Registering a FortiVoice product and downloading the license file", and "Uploading the license file to FortiVoice"; FortiVoice Phone System 8.0.0 Administration Guide, "Configuring IP extensions" (License allocation)

Prerequisite: A third-party phone license (FVE-3RDPARTY-10 or FVE-3RDPARTY-100), registered and uploaded, for each supported or generic third-party phone
What it enables: Use of third-party phones with FortiVoice 7.2 and later
How to put it in place: Register the license and download the license file in FortiCloud; GUI: Dashboard > Status (License Information widget, Update License)
Source: FortiVoice 8.0 Solution Guide, "Licensing and provisioning of third-party phone models" (in FortiVoice 7.2.x, a supported or generic third-party phone needs the registered license) and "FortiVoice add-on features" (Third-Party Phone)

Prerequisite: A call center license (FVE-CALLC-BASE, with FVE-CALLC-10 or FVE-CALLC-100 for more agents), registered and uploaded
What it enables: Call center reports and their retention settings
How to put it in place: Register the license and download the license file in FortiCloud; GUI: Dashboard > Status (License Information widget, Update License)
Source: FortiVoice Phone System 8.0.0 Administration Guide, "Configuring system capacity" (Call Center Report requires the call center license); FortiVoice 8.0 Solution Guide, "FortiVoice add-on features" (Call Center)

Prerequisite: FortiCare Premium Support registered to the FortiVoice unit (it adds the Firmware and General Updates entitlement), and Internet access from the unit to the Fortinet cloud image server
What it enables: The firmware store for FortiFone phones and for managed FortiVoice gateways and LSG units, and every subscription license
How to put it in place: Purchase FortiCare Premium Support and register it in FortiCloud; check that GUI: Dashboard > Status (License Information widget) shows Firmware Store
Source: FortiVoice Phone System 8.0.0 Administration Guide, "Using the firmware store for FortiFone" and "Upgrading managed FortiVoice devices using the cloud server" (Prerequisites); FortiVoice 8.0 Solution Guide, "Subscription licenses" (subscription licenses require FortiCare Premium Support)

Prerequisite: A FortiCall subscription (FortiVoice 8.0.0 and later), registered and applied to a supported model: FVE-50G2, FVE-100F, FVE-200F8, FVE-500F, FVE-2000F, FVE-5000F/H, or FVE-VM-100 to FVE-VM-50000
What it enables: FortiCall VoIP trunks and DID numbers managed in the FortiVoice Cloud portal
How to put it in place: Purchase and register the subscription in the Fortinet Support portal; check the FortiCall entitlement and widget in GUI: Dashboard > Status (License Information widget)
Source: FortiVoice Phone System 8.0.0 Administration Guide, "Configuring your FortiCall service" (Supported FortiVoice models; Prerequisites); FortiVoice 8.0 Solution Guide, "Subscription licenses" (FortiCall)

Prerequisite: A FortiGate deployment that uses FortiLink, with the FortiFone deployment configured on the FortiGate
What it enables: FortiLink deployment and auto-provisioning of FortiFone endpoints from FortiGate
How to put it in place: Configure FortiLink and the FortiVoice deployment on the FortiGate (see the FortiGate documentation); there is no FortiVoice setting
Source: FortiVoice 8.0.0 release notes, "What's new" (FortiLink integration)
